cita: Guan et al. (2026). A Dual-Helix Governance Approach Towards Reliable Agentic AI for WebGIS Development.
problema: Agentic WebGIS development suffers five compounding LLM limitations -- long-context degradation, cross-session forgetting, output stochasticity, instruction-following failures, and fine-tuning's adaptation rigidity -- because current governance (prompting, RAG, fine-tuning) is purely informational/advisory, not structurally enforced.
mecanismo: A dual-helix of Knowledge Externalization (a persistent, version-controlled knowledge graph of typed JSON nodes -- Category/Concept/Document -- each linking to a Markdown file) and Behavioral Enforcement (executable, prioritized protocol nodes an agent must validate against before executing a skill) intersect in a Skills track; role separation (meta-level Agent Builder vs task-level Domain Expert) prevents context contamination, and a 5-step self-learning cycle (discover-structure-link-validate-persist) writes new discoveries back into the graph as auditable nodes.
evaluacion: Two case studies: (1) a real WebGIS refactor (FutureShorelines) measured via SLOC/cyclomatic-complexity/maintainability-index/JSHint-warnings before vs after governance-guided refactoring, plus KG substrate growth tracking; (2) a controlled 3-condition (unguided/static-prompt/dual-helix) 5-trial COVID-19 cartography experiment scored on 6 dimensions (E1-E6, deterministic checks + gpt-5.2 LLM-as-judge), comparing mean and standard deviation via Welch's t-test and Cohen's d.
numeros_clave: -51% cyclomatic complexity, -49% logical SLOC, +7pt maintainability index, -98% JSHint warnings (Table 3, FutureShorelines refactor); dual-helix condition sigma=0.36 vs static-prompt baseline sigma=0.79 (variance more than halved, Sec.5); rule-compliance dimension E5 mean 1.66 vs 1.30 baseline (+27.7%); Welch t(5.18)=1.60 p=0.169, Cohen's d=0.46; KG substrate grew up to 433% (Table 4).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The KG node taxonomy (Category/Concept/Document, JSON + linked Markdown, version-controlled, Sec.3.2 Table 2) offers a concrete Tier-1 typed-narrative pattern MF could mirror for docs-as-truth.
The Domain Expert's mandatory 'plan-first' step with human approval gate before autonomous execution (Sec.3.3) is a concrete plan-state-as-memory pattern.
The 5-step self-learning cycle (discover-structure-link-validate-persist, Sec.3.4, Fig.4) is an explicit discretionary write trigger fired on discovery, not a blind append.
KG substrate growth (Table 4, up to 433% node growth) demonstrates promotion of transient discoveries (e.g. vector-tile fallback logic) into durable graph nodes, matching MF's consolidation need.

notes: Sec.4.4 Table 3 (FutureShorelines refactor code-quality metrics) and Sec.5 Fig.8 + rule-compliance table (variance reduction / E5 results) anchor the numbers above.

cita: Xu et al. (2025). Everything is Context: Agentic File System Abstraction for Context Engineering.
problema: Agentic GenAI context management (memory, tools, external knowledge, human input) via prompt engineering/RAG/tool integration remains fragmented and ad hoc, producing transient, opaque, unverifiable context artefacts that cause context rot and knowledge drift.
mecanismo: A Unix-'everything is a file' abstraction mounts heterogeneous context sources (KGs, memory stores, human notes, MCP tools) into one governed namespace with uniform metadata/access-control; a Persistent Context Repository layers History (immutable append-only log), Memory (indexed/structured views -- episodic, fact, experiential, procedural, user -- built by summarisation/embedding/clustering), and Scratchpad (ephemeral per-task workspace, later pruned or promoted into Memory/History); a Context Engineering Pipeline (Constructor/Updater/Evaluator) then selects, compresses, and incrementally streams this repository into the bounded token window, logging every transition for traceability.
evaluacion: Systems paper with no quantitative benchmark: validated through architectural description plus two exemplars implemented in the open-source AIGNE framework -- a memory-enabled conversational agent (afs_list/afs_read tool calls building a context manifest) and an MCP-mounted GitHub assistant demonstrating any MCP server can be exposed as a file-system module.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: History is explicitly the 'immutable source of truth' from which Memory (indexed/derived views) is built via summarisation/embedding -- the same truth-vs-derived split MF encodes as TIER-DOCS/TIER-INDICE (Sec.IV, Sec.IV-B).
Memory is described as 'structured and indexed views' over History, exposed per agent/session and rebuildable from the immutable log -- a derived-cache role matching MF's Tier-3 (Sec.IV-B).
Memory deduplication/consolidation strategies are named as a required mitigation for stateless-session memory growth and redundancy (Sec.V-A.2), a concrete consolidation trigger MF could adopt.
Every file-system transaction (agent or human) is logged with timestamp/origin/lineage for provenance and post-hoc audit (Sec.III.4), directly extending MF's provenance/staleness need.

notes: Sec.IV/Sec.IV-A-D (History/Memory/Scratchpad lifecycle, Table I taxonomy) and Sec.VI exemplars (memory agent, GitHub MCP) are the qualitative anchors; purely CUALITATIVA, no benchmark numbers reported.

cita: Vasilopoulos, A. (2026). Codified Context: Infrastructure for AI Agents in a Complex Codebase.
problema: Single-file agent manifests (.cursorrules/CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md) don't scale beyond modest codebases -- a 100,000-line system can't be described in one prompt -- so AI coding agents keep losing project conventions, coherence, and past mistakes across sessions in large, multi-agent codebases.
mecanismo: A three-tier codified-context infrastructure: Tier-1 hot-memory 'constitution' (~660-line Markdown, always loaded, encodes conventions + orchestration trigger tables routing tasks to agents); Tier-2 19 specialized domain-expert agent specs (~9,300 lines, embedding >50% project-specific domain knowledge, symptom-cause-fix tables) invoked per task via the trigger table; Tier-3 cold-memory knowledge base of 34 Markdown subsystem docs (~16,250 lines) retrieved on demand through an MCP keyword-search server (list_subsystems/find_relevant_context/suggest_agent); all three tiers overlap intentionally to counter 'brevity bias' collapse toward generic prompts.
evaluacion: Systems/experience-report paper: quantitative infrastructure-growth and interaction metrics mined from Git history and 1,457 JSONL conversation logs across 283 development sessions (no controlled ablation), complemented by four observational case studies (save-system coordination, UI-sync captured experience, drop-system gap detection, deterministic-RNG debugging) with no causal claims.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The 3-tier hot/warm/cold memory (Tier1 always-loaded constitution, Tier2 specialist-agent docs, Tier3 34 on-demand Markdown specs, ~26,200 lines total, Table 3) is a measured instance of docs-as-typed-truth scaling beyond a single manifest -- strong external confirmation of MF's TIER-DOCS bet.
Each Tier-3 document is explicitly 'scoped to a single subsystem' (Sec.3.3) -- a single-source-per-fact seam discipline MF's COSTURAS anchor could adopt verbatim.

Agent Tier-2 specs are created reactively when 'a category of task repeatedly required re-explaining the same domain knowledge' (Sec.3.2 Emergence pattern) -- codifying recurring gotchas into a durable spec.
Retrieval usage is directly measured (1,478 MCP retrieval calls across 218 sessions, 194 agent conversations reading KB docs, Sec.4.4) rather than assumed, matching MF's measured-retrieval need.

notes: Sec.4.2-4.4 (Table 3 infra scale 24.2% knowledge/code ratio, 283 sessions, 2,801 human prompts, 1,197 agent invocations) and the 4 case studies (Sec.4.4.1-4.4.4) anchor the qualitative evidence; purely CUALITATIVA per extraction, no ablation numbers.

cita: Fan et al. (2026). Skill Drift Is Contract Violation: Proactive Maintenance for LLM Agent Skill Libraries.
problema: Reusable LLM agent skill documents silently decay as the external services/APIs/packages/configs they reference evolve, but existing monitors observe raw environmental values (URLs, version strings) rather than the operational role those values play in a skill, forcing a bad trade-off between false alarms and missed drift.
mecanismo: SkillGuard reframes skill drift as contract violation: a deterministic pass extracts candidate environment mentions (15 pattern families -- URLs, versions, imports, API paths, auth, Docker images, env vars...), then a semantic pass labels each as an executable contract record (type, role in {OPERATIONAL, INCIDENTAL}, value, evidence span); only OPERATIONAL contracts are matched against known/live drift events via a type-gated predicate, and a violated contract becomes a localized repair specification (failed assumption + evidence span + old/new value) fed back to the LLM for targeted, verifiable repair.
evaluacion: Evaluated on the released DriftBench (880 pairs: 174 controlled drifts, 107 real-world drifts from live registries/changelogs, 599 no-drift/hard-negative controls, 99.6% adjudicated validity + 20% human audit) across five backbone LLMs on known-drift precision/recall, a pre-registered 49-real-skill live-discovery study, and a repair-success comparison against no-localization/plain-drift-text/Self-refine/full-drift-spec baselines.
numeros_clave: Contract-free CI probes: 40% FPR; SkillGuard: 0% FPR over 599 no-drift/hard-negative cases (Wilson 95% CI [0,0.6]%), 100% precision / 76% recall (strongest backbone, Table 2); live pre-registered scan of 49 real skills: 86% conservative precision, 55% recall; repair success 10% -> 78% with contract localization (~10K tokens/skill vs ~18K for 3-round Self-refine).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: SkillGuard treats each skill doc's environment mentions as role-typed (OPERATIONAL vs INCIDENTAL) contract records rather than plain text -- a typed-narrative discipline MF's Tier-1 docs could adopt to flag load-bearing obligations vs incidental prose (Sec.4.1).

Directly measures doc staleness/drift as the central failure mode and shows contract-typed validation eliminates false alarms (0% FPR over 599 cases) while catching 76% of known drift -- confirms MF's staleness detection needs typed, role-aware checks over raw diffing (Table 2, Sec.5.1).

Proactive, precision-first drift detection (before execution failure) is a concrete discretionary write/update trigger MF's G-M1 could model -- detect violated contract, then localize and repair (Sec.4.3).

Contract-localized repair is cheaper: ~10K tokens/skill vs ~18K for 3-round Self-refine while matching its 78-80% one-round success (Sec.5.3) -- evidence that targeted/typed context beats brute-force iteration.

notes: Sec.5.1 Table 2 (known-drift precision/recall by backbone) + Sec.5.2 Fig.4 (49-skill live scan) + Sec.5.3 Fig.4B (repair success) are the numeric anchors.

cita: Pedada, S., Dhavala, A., & Patil, N. (2026). Shared Selective Persistent Memory for Agentic LLM Systems.
problema: Agentic LLM systems that generate/edit artifacts through multi-turn tool use are stateless -- each session discards the domain constraints, data schemas, tool configs, and output-format preferences that made the prior session productive, forcing costly re-specification, while naively persisting entire conversation histories is token-inefficient and actively degrades output quality via irrelevant/stale context.
mecanismo: Shared selective persistent memory decomposes reusable session knowledge into four orthogonal, git-versioned categories per workspace -- task specifications (system-prompt rules), data schemas (precomputed statistical profiles instead of raw data), tool configurations, and output constraints (a runtime data-injection contract) -- while explicitly discarding reasoning traces, tool-invocation logs, and error-recovery paths; workspaces are shareable across users under role-based access control, and a zero-token data-refresh mechanism swaps compatible data into the artifact without any LLM re-invocation.
evaluacion: Four studies: a controlled 24-task ablation (no-memory vs full-history vs selective memory) across three enterprise use cases scored by two blinded raters (kappa=0.91) with Fisher's exact significance tests; a 4-public-dataset / 36-trial replication for generalizability; a token-efficiency comparison of raw/truncated/summary-driven data representation; and a 12-participant counterbalanced user study.
numeros_clave: Selective memory: 96% task completion vs 79% no-memory vs 71% full-history (Table 1, Fisher p=0.046/0.008); public-dataset replication: 100% completion at 0 LLM tokens on 12/12 zero-token-refresh trials (Table 2); summary-driven data representation cuts tokens 97x (enterprise) to 946x (public datasets) vs raw injection (Table 3); user study: 14x faster recurring generation (12s vs 165s).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Workspace memory is decomposed into four typed, git-versioned categories (task specs, schemas, tool configs, output constraints) rather than a single freeform doc -- a category-typed narrative pattern MF's Tier-1 could extend beyond one STATE.md (Sec.3.2-3.3, Eq.3).

Summary-driven schemas cut token cost 97-946x vs raw data injection and zero-token refresh needs 0 LLM tokens on 12/12 trials (Table 2/3) -- strong confirmation that MF's context-economy discipline (derived summaries over raw dumps) pays off.

Selective forgetting is an explicit, enumerated write-time decision (discard reasoning traces/tool logs/error-recovery paths, keep 4 stable categories, Sec.3.3) -- a concrete discretionary write/discard trigger MF's G-M1 anchor could formalize.

Measures that stale session traces actively bias ('trace anchoring') the agent toward wrong prior solution paths, degrading completion 8-25pp below no-memory (Table 1/2, Sec.6.2-6.3) -- direct evidence for MF's staleness/poisoning concern in FIDELIDAD.

notes: Sec.6.2 Table 1 (24-task enterprise ablation), Sec.6.3 Table 2 (public replication), Sec.6.4 Table 3/Fig.2 (token efficiency) anchor the numbers; Sec.7 explicitly frames full-history persistence as counterproductive, not merely unhelpful.

cita: Holt et al. (2023). L2MAC: Large Language Model Automatic Computer for Extensive Code Generation.
problema: LLMs are constrained by a fixed context window, so they cannot produce long, internally-consistent outputs (e.g. large codebases): existing memory-augmented approaches only read from memory (reducing updates to append-only concatenation) or use narrow domain-specific memories (dictionaries/databases) that don't generalize and can't recover from errors.
mecanismo: L2MAC is a stored-program-computer (von Neumann) framework: an LLM 'processor' executes one instruction at a time from an LLM-generated instruction registry I, while a Control Unit manages the processor's bounded context (P1: always includes the current unresolved instruction plus prior-execution summary, decluttering as the window fills), grants precise read/write/extend access to an external file-store memory (P2), and checks each output for syntactic validity and self-generated-unit-test pass/fail before accepting the write, triggering iterative corrective regeneration on failure (P3).
evaluacion: Benchmarked Code-L2MAC against AutoGPT, CodeT, Self-Refine, Reflexion and single-shot GPT-4 on three system-design codebase-generation tasks (Features%/# Errors/LOC/Tests-Passed averaged over 10 seeds with 95% CIs) plus the standard HumanEval benchmark, and ran targeted ablations isolating P1 (context retention), P2 (read/write precision) and P3 (error-correction) contributions.
numeros_clave: Code-L2MAC: 90.2% Pass@1 on HumanEval (state-of-the-art); Table 2 URL-shortener task Features% 91.6+-8.22 vs GPT4 53.6+-10.5 / CodeT 52.9+-6.74 / Self-Refine 47.9+-8.53 / Reflexion 38.8+-6.02 / AutoGPT 25.3+-19.6, with 0+-0 syntax errors vs baselines' >=0.05.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The file store is the persistent memory of record that every instruction-agent reads/writes precisely (P2) rather than an ephemeral conversation buffer -- a docs/files-as-truth substrate MF's Tier-1 already assumes (Sec.3, Fig.2).

The Control Unit maintains an explicit instruction registry I (the decomposed task plan) and tracks per-instruction completion state across the whole run -- literal plan-state-as-memory, confirming MF's PLAN-ESTADO anchor (Sec.1, Fig.1).

P2 (precise read/write for the entire memory store) is directly measured via the Features%/error/LOC/tests-passed metrics (Table 2), showing task-oriented, checked retrieval outperforms read-only or full-context baselines -- a measured retrieval layer matching G-M2.

The Control Unit's P3 (checking generated output via syntax checkers + self-generated unit tests before accepting a memory write) is a concrete write-time fidelity gate MF could extend to docs/state writes (Sec.3, Sec.6.2 Fig.3b).

notes: Sec.6.1 Table 2 (Features%/Errors/LOC across 3 system-design tasks + HumanEval) and Sec.6.2 Fig.3 (P1/P2/P3 insight ablations) anchor the numbers; plan_estado=SI reflects the explicit instruction registry I as a persisted plan (Sec.3, Fig.1).
